A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUB framework and ATS algorithm. All 13 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including figures, equations, references, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations comparing algorithms on conference recommendation and modeled COVID-19 vaccine testing, alongside teacher-noise estimation and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results, including algorithm comparisons, teacher-noise estimation, and the analyses in Appendices B, C, E, and F.

M1.justification: The written HUB-POMDP teacher-query reward changes from f^a in v1 Definition 3.1 to -f^a in v2 Definition 4.1. This local model revision conflicts with retained negative query costs; an implemented change is not established. Algorithm 1, the POMCPOW procedure, rollout policy, and teacher-noise inference otherwise remain equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same conference-recommendation tasks, modeled vaccine-testing task, and teacher-noise estimation scenario. Moving existing experiments into appendices adds no dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Naive[50], Naive[100], Naive[200], Random, and Random Arms. Specific/general teacher selection and the best-arm, random-arm, and random-action rollout comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The experimental sections retain the 1000-step budgets, task construction, teacher rationalities and costs, discretization settings, and reward, action-frequency, and L2-loss metrics. No revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The specific/general teacher-selection comparison, rollout-policy comparison, query-cost sensitivity analysis, and teacher-noise estimation experiment are retained. v1 Figure 6 becomes v2 Figure 7 in Appendix B; the rollout and cost analyses move from Appendices C/D to E/F.

E5.justification: Both retain 25 runs on 20 recommendation problems, 25 vaccine-task runs, and 100 teacher-noise simulations. Figure 4 retains the same median, IQR, whisker, and outlier conventions. No experimental uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All 19 embedded figure panels are identical across versions after matching relocated figures. The teacher-noise estimation MSE remains 0.061. Experimental result entries, plotted rankings, and trends are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.2 and Theorems 4.2–4.3, claiming upper and lower teacher-query complexity bounds, with new proofs in Appendices D.2–D.3. This substantially expands the theoretical content. The earlier convergence and teacher-noise inference results remain as Theorems 3.2 and 4.4, with equivalent rescaling notation for the latter.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims retain the same scope: HUB formalizes teacher selection, ATS selects when and whom to query, and the two application domains support its utility. The added theoretical subsection does not redefine these central contribution claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that teachers share one utility function and excludes balancing competing values from scope, referring readers to social choice research. Its conclusion also makes the proposed scaling direction more concrete through state abstractions and hierarchical options. Existing experimental interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 Figure 8 drops v1's disclosure that the vaccine-result curves were smoothed over 10 steps. This removes a small reproducibility detail without establishing changed preprocessing. The Julia-library access statement and principal implementation and parameter information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds a crowdsourcing discussion citing Dawid and Skene, Raykar et al., and Rodrigues et al., plus Conitzer et al. for competing human values. Existing bandit, IRL, and CIRL positioning is retained despite relocation.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it introduces Preliminaries, divides related work between that section and Appendix A, moves detailed experimental discussions into Appendices B/C, and consolidates proofs in Appendix D. It also rewrites explanatory passages and updates affiliations, acknowledgements, and citation style.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one-column to two-column layout. Existing figures are resized and relocated, including teacher-selection and vaccine-result figures moved into appendices. Figure 10 changes from three panels in one row to a two-row arrangement. These are extensive presentation changes using unchanged figure content.

improvement.justification: The clearer background and explicit shared-utility limitation help, but v2 introduces formal reliability problems. The new complexity proofs do not establish their claimed guarantees: Appendix D.2 substitutes a point-probability condition for the required confidence statement, and D.3 uses the wrong inequality direction when dividing by log(1-p). The reward-sign change also conflicts with retained negative costs. These problems outweigh the limited explanatory gains, while the original empirical contribution remains intact.
